column1: # Shared boolean-flag vectors for GPY_* environment switches. `1/true/yes/on`
# is on and `0/false/no/off` is off, case-insensitive, with no surrounding
# whitespace; anything else counts as unset (the caller's default applies).
# Read by ALL FOUR implementations so they cannot drift apart:
# Format: one vector per line, tab-separated: value<TAB>state (on|off|unset).
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. No value is padded with
# whitespace: Rust's parse_flag trims, the shells do not. The single
# whole-column token \e means the EMPTY string (an empty column would be
# collapsed by bash/zsh `read`). Every reader MUST fail if this file is
# Rust maps a row to a state with parse_flag(Some(value), true) and
# parse_flag(Some(value), false): equal results mean on (true) or off (false);
# different results mean unset. Shells call __gpy_flag_value with both
# defaults and apply the same rule.
